lit-cat.note: base grammar: the three-byte literal. Fourteen patterns spell this language or a superset of it with one construct added (`(cat)`, `(?<w>cat)`, `\x63at`, `(?x) c a t`, `ca(?#comment)t`, `(?n)(ca)t`, `c\Xt`, ...); their cost minus this one's is the construct's

anc-dollar.note: end of subject OR before a final newline: `item done\n` is the edge

anc-a-uc.note: start of subject, the escape spelling

anc-z-uc.note: end of subject or before a final newline, like `$` outside (?m)

anc-z-lc.note: end of subject ONLY: rejects `item done\n` where `\Z` and `$` take it

anc-g-uc.note: the search start: find-all counts consecutive hits from the cursor

anc-m-caret.note: `^` after an internal newline under multiline

anc-m-dollar.note: `$` before an internal newline under multiline

asr-wb.note: word boundary both sides: `concatenate` is the designed miss

asr-nwb.note: NOT a word boundary both sides: `cat` alone is the designed miss

asr-k-uc.note: reset the reported start: the span begins after `key=`

cls-w.note: a word run; C-locale tables, so a Latin-1 byte ends it

cls-n-uc.note: any byte but newline, unaffected by (?s): `item` and `itxm`, never across a line end

cls-posix.note: a POSIX class: ASCII letters only under the default tables

cls-negset.note: base grammar: a negated bracket class (`cat` misses, `cxt` hits)

cls-range.note: base grammar: a bracket class of three ranges

cls-dot.note: base grammar: `.` (any byte but newline without (?s))

cls-fold-pair.note: FOLD-PAIR WITNESS: a two-member class that IS an ASCII fold pair; the same language as `(?i:a)` in the middle of `cat`

cls-pair-ctl.note: FOLD-PAIR WITNESS (the control): a two-member class that is NOT a fold pair -- the same class SIZE as `c[aA]t`, a different set

cls-mixed-case.note: FOLD-PAIR WITNESS: a mixed-case ranged class (52 members, every letter's fold pair present)

cls-i-class.note: FOLD-PAIR WITNESS: `(?i)` over a CLASS (the option folds the class and the literals both); `mod-i` is the option over a literal

qnt-plus.note: base grammar: greedy plus, the body the possessive/atomic shapes are read against

qnt-lazy.note: base grammar: lazy star inside quotes (bench/bounded carries the counted forms)

qnt-poss-plus.note: possessive plus with a body it can NEVER match (the plus keeps the last `a`): every subject is a miss, and `qnt-plus-ctl` is the control

qnt-plus-ctl.note: the CONTROL for `a++ab`: the same text minus the possessive suffix, which matches `aaab`

qnt-poss-quest.note: possessive optional: needs two `a`s (the first is kept)

grp-cap.note: a capturing group around the plain word (the `bare` row)

grp-noncap.note: a non-capturing group under a repeat

grp-named.note: a named group, angle spelling; the other two spellings are exercised by the named backreference and the python-style call

grp-atomic-rep.note: an atomic group over a repeat: same language as `a+b`

grp-atomic-alt.note: an atomic group over an alternation: FAILS on `abc` (the first branch is committed) where `(?:a|ab)c` would match

grp-comment.note: a comment group: the language is `cat`

grp-branch-reset.note: a branch-reset group: both alternatives capture as group 1

grp-callout.note: a numbered callout with no callout function installed: the language is `cat`

alt-two.note: base grammar: a two-branch literal alternation (bench/altwide carries the width ladder)

alt-nested.note: base grammar: two nested alternations, the same language as `cat|dog` plus `cog` and `dat`

bak-1.note: a numbered backreference: a doubled word

bak-2.note: two backreferences in reverse order: a four-byte palindrome

bak-g-rel.note: a relative backreference: the same language as `bak-1`

bak-k-named.note: a named backreference: a tag pair closed by its own name

bak-py.note: the python-style named backreference: the same language as `bak-1`

lka-nonatomic.note: non-atomic positive lookahead over a literal: the same language as `item`

lka-verb.note: the alpha spelling of `lka-pos`: the same language, a different spelling

rec-1.note: recursion into group 1: the same language as `rec-r-uc`, the call target being the group and not the root

rec-name.note: recursion into a named group: the same language as `rec-r-uc`

rec-g-angle.note: a subroutine call by number, angle spelling: four digits

rec-py.note: the python-style subroutine call: the same language as `rec-g-angle`

rec-fwd.note: a relative call FORWARD to the group to its right: four digits

rec-back.note: a relative call BACK to the group to its left: four digits

mod-s.note: dotall: the `.` spans the newline in `item\ndone`; NO unbounded repeat under (?s) anywhere in this set

mod-n.note: no auto-capture: the plain group stops capturing

mod-u-uc.note: ungreedy: the same language as `qnt-lazy` by inverting `+`

mod-j-uc.note: duplicate names allowed: the backreference resolves to whichever `w` set

mod-a.note: ASCII-restricted class escapes: under the default tables `\w` is already ASCII, so the same language as `cls-w`

mod-r.note: caseless restricted to one script: in byte mode the same language as `mod-i`

mod-reset.note: reset all options mid-pattern: `Cat` yes, `CAT` no

mod-unset.note: unset one option mid-pattern: the same language as `mod-reset`

esc-cr.note: carriage return + newline as two escapes: `msc-r-uc` is the one-token spelling of the same pair

esc-hex.note: a bare two-digit hex escape: the language is `cat`

esc-hex-braced.note: the braced hex spelling of a Latin-1 byte (the seed's `\x41` row names both spellings)

esc-octal-o.note: the braced octal escape: the language is `cat`

esc-octal-0.note: the `\0dd` octal escape (never a backreference): a space

esc-quote.note: literal quoting: the parentheses are bytes

msc-r-uc.note: any newline sequence: `\n` and `\r\n` both, as one token

msc-x-uc.note: an extended grapheme cluster: one byte in byte mode

unp-p-lc.note: letters by Unicode property: Latin-1 letters included, unlike `\w`

vrb-accept.note: end the match early: the span is `item`, `done` never runs

vrb-skip.note: on failure after the verb, skip the search to the verb's position

floor.note: requirements 5's per-call control: one literal byte, in `#42` and the order line only, absent from every run
